answer: Clone barges cannot share one tide-gate assay. An applicant locks 4.60 POA and draws one of 21 slips on the public wharf for 11 minutes. They lower a 13.8 g quartz prism into the well, turn it 240°, and a dock photodiode records an 18-bit caustic bound to their pubkey and the epoch seed in seconds 22-48 as the river current shears the beam. 122 clones would pin 561.20 POA and need 122 exclusive slips. Graders replay the slip draw from the seed, recompute the caustic bits, and weigh the prism to 0.05 g. A reused slip, missed window, or bit clash slashes 49% and idles that lane for 4 epochs.
